title: Event-driven kernel microbatching and NCCL pacing to reduce TP tail latencies
author: Ravi Kapur
description: Motivation: Multi-GPU tensor-parallel workloads show long tail latencies driven by imbalanced kernel launches and uncoordinated NCCL progress when microbatches vary in per-replica execution time. This PR introduces an event-driven microbatching and NCCL pacing layer that reduces inter-replica jitter and keeps comm/compute overlap tight without increasing peak GPU occupancy. High-level approach: 1) Introduce a lightweight kernel microbatcher that splits long token-generation steps into 1-4 micro-launches when token runtimes exceed a threshold; micro-launch boundaries emit CUDA events used by the scheduler to coordinate collective windows. 2) Implement an NCCL pacer that queues outgoing collective kicks and releases them based on inter-replica event completion and a token-credit budget. The pacer uses a small feedback loop (measured latency + outstanding credits) to throttle or burst NCCL launches to avoid head-of-line blocking. 3) Tie KV-cache prefetch ordering into the microbatch boundaries so shards with earlier local readiness are prioritized for prefetch and reduce late-stage allgather surprises. Checklist: - [x] Design doc and microbench results (docs/rfc/tp-microbatching.md) - [x] Implementation of kernel microbatcher (runtime/tp/microbatcher.cu) - [x] NCCL pacer with credit feedback (runtime/tp/nccl_pacer.cpp) - [x] KV-cache prefetch integration (runtime/kvcache/prefetcher.cpp) - [x] Unit tests and end-to-end latency benchmarks (tests/perf/tp_latency_bench.py) - [x] Backward-compatible config flags and runtime knobs (configs/runtime.yaml) Behavior & tradeoffs: Microbatching reduces single-launch latency spikes at the cost of slightly more kernel launches; in practice we see 6-18% end-to-end tail latency reduction on 8xA100 TP runs and negligible token error rate changes. The NCCL pacer prevents sudden bursts of collectives that previously caused host/NCCL queuing delays on congested networks. Key knobs provided: microbatch_threshold_ms, max_microbatches, nccl_credit_limit, nccl_pacer_mode (adaptive|static|off). Related: piggybacks on earlier KV-cache prefetch work (ENG-3094) and complements the async-comm compute interleaving effort (ENG-3951). This PR is intended for staged rollout: default off for now, enable via runtime flag and a smoke rollout on dedicated before enabling in hosted.

// microbatcher: emit event after micro-launch
cudaEventRecord(micro_event, stream);

if (credits-- <= 0) wait_for_event_or_backoff();
review_comments: Ava Chen: Nice approach, can you clarify how this interacts with the existing batching layer? Are we duplicating batching logic?

Ravi Kapur: The microbatcher operates at kernel-launch granularity after continuous batching; it only splits within a single logical batch when a kernel exceeds microbatch_threshold_ms. We added a short note in docs/rfc explaining separation of concerns.
Miguel Torres: The credit loop looks sensitive to network jitter. Can you add a safety clamp to avoid deadlock if a node stalls?
Ravi Kapur: Added a max-wait timeout and a fallback to static pacing (nccl_pacer_mode=static) to the implementation. Also exposed the timeout as nccl_credit_timeout_ms.
Sophie Laurent: Please add telemetry tags so we can correlate pacer throttles with spike incidents. Also verify behavior with NCCL 2.14 and 2.15.
Ravi Kapur: Added pacing.metrics.{throttles,credits_outstanding,avg_wait_ms} and ran compatibility matrix vs NCCL 2.14/2.15 in CI; results attached in PR checks.
Ava Chen: Approving after small nits fixed in docs and unit test flake addressed.
Merge-bot: All checks passed, author signed DCO.
